text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.3% today, bouncing back after a sharp four-day decline that wiped out 5.3% of its value. The recovery came as oil markets stabilized on news of potential talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global crude shipments—which eased some of the geopolitical tension that had been driving prices down earlier in the week. Crude prices also gained ground as traders assessed reports that Asian imports are climbing to their highest levels since the Iran conflict began, signaling ongoing demand.

The broader backdrop remains volatile: US oil is trading at $96.41 per barrel while global crude sits much higher at $114.89, reflecting tight supply from the conflict zone. Simultaneously, diesel prices have spiked to $6.51 per gallon nationally, prompting industry warnings against Trump's proposed diesel export ban—a political debate that adds uncertainty for refiners like ConocoPhillips, though higher energy costs can support their margins in the near term.
